common_name: Picotee Amaryllis (Classic White Amaryllis with Thin Red Picotee Edge)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in spring with the neck at or just above soil surface; Picotee is one of the most recognizable amaryllis cultivars, prized for its crisp white petals rimmed in a thin band of red.

directions: Plant bulbs in fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade to morning sun, with the neck of the bulb at or just above the soil surface. Picotee bears large, pure white flowers finely edged in a thin, crisp band of red along each petal margin, a clean and elegant picotee pattern that has made it one of the most widely sold and recognizable amaryllis cultivars for both garden display and holiday forcing. In zone 8-10 gardens it can be left in the ground year-round, naturalizing and multiplying into an increasingly full clump over the years. Allow foliage to grow and die back naturally after flowering rather than cutting it early, since the leaves recharge the bulb, and for container forcing plant with roughly a third of the bulb exposed above the potting mix for traditional winter bloom indoors.
sources: Louisiana State University AgCenter
University of Florida IFAS Extension — Amaryllis
